findings.recommendation: Keep allowUniversalAccessFromFileURLs disabled and serve local content from a constrained WebViewAssetLoader origin when possible.

findings.description: Remote content invoked a native JavaScript bridge method. This is a direct native attack surface from web content.

findings.description: The WebView loaded content over HTTP. Cleartext traffic can be intercepted or modified, which is especially dangerous when JavaScript bridges are exposed.
findings.recommendation: Use HTTPS for WebView content and disable cleartext traffic in the Android network security configuration.

findings.description: A page loaded from file:// can read other file:// resources, which can expose local app or device files.

findings.description: The WebView loaded local file content. file:// pages are risky when file access or JavaScript bridges are enabled.
findings.recommendation: Avoid file:// content for untrusted pages. Prefer WebViewAssetLoader or a tightly controlled HTTPS origin.

findings.description: A native object was exposed to JavaScript through addJavascriptInterface. Any page that can run JavaScript in this WebView can attempt to call annotated public methods.
findings.recommendation: Expose bridges only to trusted origins, remove the bridge before loading untrusted content, and enforce origin checks in every sensitive method.
findings.title: JavaScript bridge exposed to WebView content

findings.description: A native object was exposed to JavaScript through addJavascriptInterface. Any page that can run JavaScript in this WebView can attempt to call annotated public methods.

findings.description: The WebView allows HTTPS pages to load cleartext HTTP subresources, weakening transport security.
findings.recommendation: Use MIXED_CONTENT_NEVER_ALLOW unless a documented legacy compatibility case exists.
